package_info.why_malicious: The provided ENISA threat landscape report is a high-level summary of cybersecurity trends and does not analyze or describe any specific malicious software package. It discusses general threat categories (e.g., ransomware, supply chain attacks, info stealers, weaponized AI) and attack techniques, but does not provide concrete package names, code, or technical details about individual malware samples.

behavioral_signatures: Use of legitimate cloud services (e.g., GitHub, Vimeo, Google Cloud Run, Cloudflare Workers) for malware distribution or data exfiltration
Living Off the Land techniques: abuse of legitimate admin tools and remote management software
Automated creation of phishing content or malicious scripts using AI/LLMs
Exploitation of zero-day and one-day vulnerabilities in internet-facing services
file_indicators: No specific file indicators provided in the report
network_indicators: Connections to legitimate cloud platforms for C2 or exfiltration
Abuse of trusted domains/subdomains for malware hosting
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unusual or unauthorized use of legitimate cloud services and remote management tools, especially for data exfiltration or malware delivery. Detect anomalous network traffic to anonymizing services (VPN, TOR) and unexpected connections to cloud platforms from endpoints. Watch for automated or AI-generated phishing content and scripts. Prioritize patching of internet-facing services and monitor for exploitation attempts against known vulnerabilities. Since no specific package or code is described, detection should focus on behavioral and network patterns consistent with the threat categories outlined.
